meta.subtitle: Growth and margins keep rising, but near its 52-week high the stock already prices in consensus delivery

analystCommentary:
Red Violet's second quarter of 2026 improved on the year-ago quarter across every line the MD&A reports: revenue, gross margin, net income, adjusted EBITDA and operating cash flow all rose. Revenue has grown at double-digit rates in each of the last four fiscal years, and the operating margin has widened every year (see Financials).

The share price has moved with the results. At $79.55 on October 2, 2026, the stock sat close to its 52-week high of $81.80, against a low of $33.40. At that price the shares offer a thin cash yield and little room above the Street's targets (see Valuation).

The August 2026 equity offering adds a second question: what the company does with the new cash (see Management). We rate RDVT HOLD.

executiveSummary.companyOverview:
Red Violet, Inc. is an analytics and information solutions company that delivers identity intelligence in the United States. Its cloud-native platform, CORE, combines extensive public and proprietary data assets with machine learning to identify and locate people, businesses, assets and their interrelationships.

The company markets its solutions mainly through two brands. IDI's flagship product, idiCORE, is an investigative solution used for due diligence, risk mitigation, identity authentication and regulatory compliance by financial services companies, insurers, law enforcement and government, law firms, collections and others. FOREWARN is an app-based solution, currently tailored for the real estate industry, that gives professionals information about a consumer before a face-to-face meeting.

Red Violet reports a single segment, generates substantially all of its revenue from licensing its solutions, and is headquartered in Boca Raton, Florida.

thesis.body: The business case is good: double-digit revenue growth, an operating margin that has widened every year, and FY25 free cash flow above net income. The valuation case is weaker. The price already discounts consensus delivery, so our Base case adds only modest upside, while a re-rating to a lower multiple would cost far more than continued delivery would add (see Valuation). We rate the shares HOLD rather than BUY.

catalysts: How management deploys the proceeds of the August 2026 equity offering, including any acquisition (see Management).
Third-quarter 2026 results, and whether revenue growth stays ahead of the FY26E consensus rate (see Growth).
Further customer growth at IDI and user growth at FOREWARN.
Revisions to FY27E consensus earnings, which anchor all three of our scenarios.
risks: A valuation that leaves little room for a slowdown (see Valuation).
A data breach or privacy incident at a company that stores sensitive consumer information.
An acquisition that overpays or proves hard to integrate.
Dilution from the August 2026 share issue.

financials.incomeCommentary:
FY25 revenue was $90.3M, up {+20.0%+}, after growth of 24.9% in FY24 and 12.9% in FY23. Operating margin has widened every year in the series, from -3.0% in FY21 to 14.6% in FY25, and FY25 net income was $13.2M, or $0.91 per diluted share. Diluted EPS has been uneven: FY23's $0.96 was above FY24's figure, and no source explains the swing, so we read the trend through the operating margin rather than EPS.

The second quarter of 2026 extended the trend. Revenue rose 23% to $26.7 million and the quarter's operating margin was 22.8%. Gross margin increased to 76% from 72%, and net income rose 85% to $5.0 million.

Adjusted figures run well ahead of reported ones. Adjusted EBITDA was $11.2 million in the quarter, a 42% margin against 35% a year earlier, but the measure excludes share-based compensation, depreciation and amortization, among other items. On a reported basis the trailing operating margin is 17.9% and the trailing net margin 16.5%. We judge the business on reported profit, and Valuation sets out what that means for the multiple.
financials.balanceCommentary:
Cash and cash equivalents were $50.0 million at June 30, 2026, and the trailing current ratio is 10.88. Our data shows no debt for FY22 to FY25; that is a gap in the data rather than a confirmed zero, though nothing in the filing excerpt points to borrowing. The balance sheet does not constrain the business.

The August 2026 equity offering (see Management) closed after the quarter end, so its proceeds are not in the June balance. The balance-sheet question is therefore not funding but how the cash is deployed.
financials.cashflowCommentary:
Free cash flow was $18.2M in FY25, a 20.2% FCF margin, after capital expenditure of -$11.2M. The margin stepped up from 9.8% in FY23 to 19.1% in FY24 and edged higher in FY25; in FY21 and FY22 it was 8.4% and 6.8%. FY25 free cash flow was above net income, but the FCF margin rose much less in FY25 than the operating margin did (see Income), so cash generation did not widen at the pace of reported profit last year.

Capital spending is a real call on cash here, and the table shows it in every year. The company's own FCF definition deducts capitalized costs included in intangible assets as well as purchases of property and equipment, so capitalized investment, not only equipment, comes out of free cash flow. In the second quarter of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities rose 42% to $10.6 million.

The business funds itself. The constraint is price: the trailing FCF yield is 1.7%, so a holder at today's value relies on growth rather than current cash return.

valuation.multiplesCommentary:
At the current price RDVT trades at 70.4x trailing earnings, 66.0x trailing EV/EBITDA and 12.9x sales. The vendor's 47.9x NTM P/E equals the price over FY26E consensus EPS of $1.66, so we treat it as today's current-year multiple; the ~45.2x on FY27E is the same price over FY27E consensus EPS of $1.76.

The earnings bases differ. The trailing multiple rests on GAAP earnings, while FY26E consensus EPS sits far above FY25 diluted EPS of $0.91 and its basis is not stated; in the second quarter the company reported GAAP diluted EPS of $0.34 and adjusted diluted EPS of $0.50. We therefore value the shares on a consensus-based multiple applied to consensus EPS, so both sides of each comparison share one basis, and we do not set forward figures against the trailing GAAP multiple.

Consensus EPS rises only at a single-digit rate from FY26E to FY27E, while consensus revenue keeps growing at a double-digit rate (see Growth). That slowdown in per-share earnings is the main argument against paying today's multiple a year out.

The Street is uniformly positive but sees limited upside: all 4 covering analysts rate Buy, with a consensus target of $84.50 (+6.2%), a median of $87.50 and a range of $73.00–$90.00. We have no peer multiples, so we judge the price against the growth path and the cash yield (see Financials).

scenarios.name: Bull
scenarios.driver: Revenue growth stays near the second-quarter pace, FY27E estimates rise, and the offering cash funds an acquisition the market sees as accretive. We apply 55x to FY27E EPS of $1.76: our assumed premium to the current-year multiple held in Base, standing in for both higher estimates and a richer rating. The result sits above the top of the Street target range.

scenarios.name: Base
scenarios.driver: The company delivers consensus, the offering cash is deployed slowly, and a year out the market still pays today's 47.9x current-year multiple, applied to the same FY27E EPS. The result lands close to the $84.50 consensus target, which serves as a separate check on the anchor.

scenarios.name: Bear
scenarios.driver: Consensus earnings are delivered, but the slower FY27E EPS growth in consensus becomes the market's focus and the multiple contracts to 30x the same FY27E EPS, a level we set as still a premium for a business with contracted revenue whose per-share earnings growth has slowed. The price falls below the bottom of the Street range but stays above the 52-week low; no earnings miss is needed.

valuation.scenarioCommentary:
Base carries the most weight because it needs only consensus delivery and an unchanged current-year multiple, and the Street's consensus target lands in the same place. The case against it is the FY27E earnings slowdown: a market that looks a year ahead may not pay today's current-year multiple for that rate of EPS growth. The multiple anchor decides the Base, and a lower Base multiple would push the result toward SELL.

Bear gets more weight than Bull, and the split is a judgment rather than a finding. For Bear: its trigger is already in consensus, the shares sit near their 52-week high after a steep rise from the low, and the trailing FCF yield is thin. For Bull: second-quarter revenue growth ran ahead of the FY26E consensus rate (see Growth), and the offering gives the company cash for acquisitions. Bull still needs estimates to rise, while Bear needs only a change in sentiment. Swapping the two weights would leave the label at HOLD.

The result is an expected upside of -2.0% and a bear-case downside of -33.6%. That is well short of the BUY threshold, and from the starting multiple the downside in Bear outweighs the upside in Bull.

Our $72–$90 target range brackets Base and the weighted fair value; its low sits near the bottom of the Street range and its high matches the top.

segments.name: Consolidated
segments.body: Red Violet reports a single segment and does not break out revenue by brand. The MD&A gives operating measures instead: as of June 30, 2026 IDI had 10,869 billable customers against 9,549 a year earlier, and FOREWARN had 443,173 users against 346,671. In the three months ended June 30, 2026, 77% of revenue was attributable to customers with pricing contracts, which are generally annual or longer with auto renewal, and 23% to transactional customers. That gives good visibility, although the company recognizes some licensing fees from a combination of a monthly fee and usage, so not all of the contracted share is fixed.

moatFactors.name: Data assets and platform
moatFactors.body: CORE pairs the company's data assets with machine learning built into the platform. Keeping such datasets and the analytics on top of them current takes continuing investment, and that investment is a standing claim on cash (see Financials). The 2025 Form 10-K, filed March 4, 2026, describes the data and analytics sector as characterized by rapidly changing technology, so this advantage lasts only as long as the investment continues.

moatFactors.name: Workflow embedding
moatFactors.body: The company's land-and-expand model starts with a trial and grows as customers add use cases across departments and become increasingly reliant on the solutions in their daily workflow. The rise in IDI billable customers and the contract structure (see Segments) are consistent with that. Renewal is still a point at which a customer can leave.

moatFactors.name: FOREWARN distribution
moatFactors.body: 660 REALTOR Associations throughout the U.S. are now contracted to use FOREWARN, which gives the product an established channel to its users. A new entrant would need time to build a comparable network. The same channel ties FOREWARN to one industry, since the MD&A describes it as currently tailored for real estate.

businessMoat.durability: We rate the moat NARROW. Widening margins and contracted, auto-renewing revenue are consistent with real customer reliance. We stop short of wide because the company is small, its data advantage depends on continued investment, and a single serious security incident could undo customer reliance (see Risks). The moat holds if CORE keeps pace with technology change and the company avoids a breach.

points: Consensus expects FY26E revenue of ~$106.7M, up 18%, slightly slower than FY25. Second-quarter growth ran ahead of that rate (see Financials), so the FY26E bar looks achievable; the price already assumes it is met.
FY27E consensus revenue of $120.8M implies slower growth again, and consensus EPS grows more slowly still (see Valuation). The path the Street models is deceleration, not acceleration.
In the second quarter, IDI added 447 customers and FOREWARN added 25,493 users. The year-over-year rise in both counts (see Moat) fits the land-and-expand model.

Acquisitions are the swing factor. The company lists potential strategic acquisitions among the uses of the offering proceeds but names no target, so any added growth is speculative until a deal is announced (see Management).

management.leadership: No proxy statement was captured for this report, so we do not name or comment on individual executives. The MD&A describes the operating approach: an inside sales team, a strategic sales team for major accounts, and distributors, resellers and strategic partners, with management continuing to build out the sales organization. The steady rise in operating margin over five years (see Financials) is the main evidence of execution available to us.
management.capitalAllocation:
Red Violet pays no dividend. Year to date through June 30, 2026 it purchased 74,500 shares at an average price of $41.87 under its Stock Repurchase Program, with $15.5 million remaining on the authorization. In August 2026 it then issued 1,916,667 new shares, including 250,000 from the underwriters' option, for net proceeds of approximately $109.0 million. That issue equals more than a tenth of the ~16.05M shares outstanding, so on net the share count rose and per-share growth now has to absorb a larger base.

Management intends to use the proceeds for working capital and general corporate purposes, including potential strategic acquisitions, and names no target. The offering pays off for existing holders only if the cash earns more than the dilution costs them. The test is what any acquisition costs relative to the revenue and cash flow it adds.
management.governance: No proxy statement was captured for this report, so we cannot assess board composition and independence, executive pay, insider ownership or related-party dealings. We make no governance claims beyond that gap, and readers should consult the company's latest proxy before relying on this section.

idiosyncratic: Data security: the 10-K says the company aggregates, stores and processes a large amount of sensitive and confidential consumer information, and that a breach could result in a material loss of business, substantial legal liability or significant harm to its reputation. It also notes that insurance policies may not cover the entire cost of a claim.

Privacy: the 10-K warns that privacy concerns or an unauthorized disclosure of personal information could harm the company's reputation, impair its ability to attract and retain customers, or subject it to claims or litigation, and that it could incur significant costs to comply with state and federal data privacy and breach-notification laws.

Technology change: the 10-K says success depends on developing new products and enhancements in a timely manner, and that the company or its competitors may introduce products that cause existing ones to become obsolete.
Capital deployment: the offering proceeds raise the risk of an overpriced or poorly integrated acquisition (see Management).
Valuation: the multiple-compression path set out in the Bear scenario.
risks.systemic: Demand from the customer groups the company serves, including financial services, insurance, collections and real estate professionals, could weaken if activity in those industries slows. A change in federal or state privacy law could also affect the whole identity-data industry at once. As a small-cap growth stock trading on a high multiple, RDVT is also exposed to shifts in market appetite for growth equities.

body: HOLD, target range $72–$90, on the scenario math in Valuation. The business is growing and widening its margins, but the price already reflects consensus delivery.

On unchanged scenarios, the label would turn BUY only at a price somewhat below the bottom of our range, and SELL at a price just above the 52-week high. Beyond price, we would revisit the call if FY27E consensus earnings rise, if the offering cash funds an acquisition that adds to per-share earnings, or if a security incident or revenue growth falling below consensus points toward the Bear case.
